newsitem.title: GERMANY: German officials criticise Schiphol tax-free role.
newsitem.headline: German officials criticise Schiphol tax-free role.

text.p: Tax-free status for Amsterdam Schiphol airport is distorting competition between European airports, German officials said.

Karl Starzacher, finance minister of the state of Hesse, which is the largest shareholder in Frankfurt airport owner Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), said pressure would be put on Brussels to look into the situation.

Speaking at the opening of a new FAG cargo terminal, he noted that Frankfurt airport was increasingly facing competition at a time when the world air cargo market was predicted to grow by eight percent a year.
"I would like to stress explicitly the readiness of the Hesse state government to support the development of (Frankfurt) airport politically," he said.
He added: "It needs to be examined to what extent the subsidising of Amsterdam airport is in accordance with EU competition law."
Frankfurt airport received no subsidies and financed all investment itself or with private partners, he said.
Starzacher added that the new FAG cargo terminal would help Frankfurt to secure its position as the top airfreight airport in Europe.
In a speech at the terminal opening, FAG chairman Wilhelm Bender said: "We say yes to competition. We demand however that the same, fair pre-conditions exist in the Europe of the EU.
"The tax exemption for Amsterdam airport or financial support for the infrastructure of others distorts the sought-after European harmonisation," he added.
